purpose: Cross-check three conflict-prone binomial labels in Quimpang et al. (2015) against Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes, preserving the article's source strings and row structure.

authority.name: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes
authority.institution: California Academy of Sciences, Institute for Biodiversity Science and Sustainability
authority.versionObserved: Online version updated 13 August 2026 on the indexed selected records.
authority.accessMethod: Selected exact-name results from official Catalog pages were reviewed through indexed excerpts. Direct opens of selected records returned access errors; no challenge or access control was bypassed.
authority.reuse: No item-specific permission to republish Catalog text was verified. Only short attributed name-status notes and URLs are retained; no bulk export or record text is reproduced.

nameCrosswalk.sourceLabel: Puntius bantolanensis (Day, 1914), listed in the paper with Barbus bantolanensis as a synonym
nameCrosswalk.authorityName: Barbus bantolanensis Day 1914 is treated as a synonym of Barbodes manguaoensis (Day 1914)
nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: Synonym crosswalk; cataloged type locality for the bantolanensis name is Lake Manguao, Palawan; Barbodes manguaoensis is listed as Palawan endemic.
nameCrosswalk.interpretation: This creates a serious conflict with reading the article's 'endemic' Mindanao record as verified. It is a nomenclatural and type-locality flag only; it cannot establish which fish the authors sampled or whether the field label was a misidentification. Preserve the historical table label and seek voucher accessions or author clarification.

nameCrosswalk.sourceLabel: Puntius binutatus (Valenciennes, 1842); the table also prints Barbus binutatus
nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: The Catalog lists Barbodes binotatus as valid and gives earlier combinations including Puntius binotatus. The exact source spelling binutatus was not located in the checked Catalog results.
nameCrosswalk.interpretation: Barbodes binotatus is a close-spelling candidate only. Do not silently correct the source label or assign the accepted name to these unvouchered samples. The Catalog's broad range is not used as a Mindanao occurrence record.

nameCrosswalk.sourceLabel: Sicyopterus lagocephalus (Pallas, 1770), printed twice in Table 1 with different common names and mountain marks
nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: Valid as printed in the Catalog.
nameCrosswalk.interpretation: The Catalog supports the name's nomenclatural status, not the duplicated table entries, common-name distinction, presence marks, counts or specimen identities. Keep both historical rows separate until vouchers or field records resolve them.

limitations: This is a targeted check of three flagged binomial labels only; other binomials and genus-level rows in the article remain unchecked.
No voucher accession numbers or item-to-site voucher crosswalks are available in the reviewed paper, so no sampled fish was independently reidentified.
Catalog range and type-locality notes are not used to infer current presence, absence, native status or waterbody-level occurrence in the study area.
The article's unresolved 34-species/five-unidentified wording and its one-unidentified-species conclusion remain as a separate source-count issue.
Taxonomic status does not resolve the article's reuse rights, current fish presence, diet, safety or legal catchability.
nextAction: If pursuing the complete table, cross-check the remaining source labels without normalizing the original strings, then seek public voucher identifiers or author clarification for the flagged Puntius and duplicate Sicyopterus rows. Do not turn this historical survey into app species or waterbody records without specimen/site evidence and separate rights review.
